subject: Urgent: Lumenity private cluster — throughput cliff, 5xx surge, exec escalation
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@lumenity.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@lumenity.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: sudden p95 and 5xx surge on private cluster (Lumenity)

Rafael —

We're seeing a sharp regression on our private VPC cluster starting ~08:50 PST. P95 latency has climbed from ~220ms to 1.2s for our inference route, and error rate (502/504) has spiked to ~7% over the last 20 minutes. Throughput dropped by ~35% even though traffic volume is stable.

We've attached sample logs and a compressed trace snapshot. Key observations from our side:
- CPU p95 on host nodes spikes correlated with 5xx bursts
- Several requests show K/V cache misses on repeated prefix patterns
- No config changes on our side since yesterday (we're on the private bundle you provisioned)

Can Redwood confirm whether any kernel/scheduler updates, scaling events, or routing fallbacks occurred on your side? This is impacting our production customers — leadership is asking for an ETA.

Attachments: lumenity-error-sample-logs.tar.gz (log archive), p95-cpu-traces.png

Elena
Elena Morales
Head of SRE, Lumenity AI
elena.morales@lumenity.ai

To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@lumenity.ai>

Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2027 11:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: sudden p95 and 5xx surge on private cluster (Lumenity)

Elena — thanks for the quick heads-up and the logs. I'm escalating this immediately.

Quick notes from our side:
- No planned runtime kernel changes or rollout in your region in the past 24h.
- Our infra telemetry shows a transient queue buildup on the private shard serving your tenant starting 08:47 PST with concurrent queue depth rising ~2.8x.
- We'll need a short window to triage batching parameters, KV cache warming, and possible contiguous memory pressure that could cause decoder stalls.

I've looped in Marissa (SRE lead for private deployments) and Laura (eng manager) to coordinate a triage.
Action items:
1) Marissa — can your team pull the full trace bundle from the Drive link and run the kernel hotpath overlay (I believe Lumenity attached the symbolized traces)?
2) Elena — can you confirm whether you saw any traffic pattern changes (longer prompts, increased function-calling) at 08:40–09:00?
3) We'll provide an interim mitigation (temporary routing to a warmed variant or short concurrency cap) while we investigate.

Rafael Mendes
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Elena Morales <elena.morales@lumenity.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Dec 2027 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: sudden p95 and 5xx surge on private cluster (Lumenity)

Folks — quick triage notes after initial trace analysis:
- The traces show decoder stall amplification tied to one decoder kernel path that hits a pointer-chasing slowdown under certain sequence alignment (we've seen this pattern with mixed-quant runs before).
- Concurrent batching on that shard surged due to an inadvertent burst from an orchestration retry loop (external). That amplified cache misses and caused memory fragmentation.

Short-term mitigations we can apply within 30 minutes (requires a brief rolling restart of 2/10 nodes):
- Force the shard to use the alternate decoder kernel (safe fallback, ~5% perf cost but removes stall surface)
- Lower max-concurrency to 60% for 10 minutes and enable aggressive prefix KV warming for frequent keys
- Temporarily route 10% of traffic to a warmed-compatible variant with slightly lower qps to prevent tail amplification

Longer-term asks for Lumenity (non-blocking):
- Share request fingerprints for the 08:40–09:00 window so we can craft targeted prefix-cache rules
- Consider limiting upstream retries in orchestration to avoid retry storms that multiply queue depth

I'm preparing a short runbook and will push the kernel switch if you approve. Rafael, Laura — if we go the rolling restart route we should schedule with the customer for a staged window (ETA to start ~11:00 PST).

Marissa Cole
SRE Lead, Private Deployments
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Anand Patil <anand.patil@lumenity.ai>

Date: Sat, 11 Dec 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: sudden p95 and 5xx surge on private cluster (Lumenity)

Marissa / Rafael — thanks for the analysis. We dug deeper and confirmed an orchestration retry loop on our side: one of our downstream services returned an intermittent 429 which caused our client to retry aggressively for ~7 minutes. We accept that contributed to the amplification.

We're attaching expanded logs and a sampling of request fingerprints for the window. We also confirm we can accept a short rolling restart and the kernel fallback; please advise on the exact start time and expected customer-visible impact.

Attachments: lumenity-error-sample-logs.tar.gz (expanded), request_fingerprints.json (sample), p95-cpu-traces.png

Anand Patil
Lead Platform Engineer, Lumenity AI
anand.patil@lumenity.ai

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Elena Morales <elena.morales@lumenity.ai>, Anand Patil <anand.patil@lumenity.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Dec 2027 18:40:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Lumenity private cluster — mitigation completed, exec summary and follow-ups

Laura / Markus — quick executive summary for visibility and any support we should offer Lumenity:

Summary of incident (timeline):
- 2027-12-10 08:47 PST — transient orchestration retries from Lumenity upstream begin; queue depth on private shard rises sharply
- 2027-12-10 09:15 PST — Lumenity reports p95 climb to ~1.2s and ~7% 5xx rate
- 2027-12-11 10:20 PST — Redwood SRE identifies decoder kernel hotpath stall under mixed-quant run amplified by cache misses and memory fragmentation
- 2027-12-11 11:05 PST — with customer approval, performed rolling restart of 2/10 nodes, switched shard to alternate decoder kernel, lowered concurrency caps, enabled aggressive KV prefix warming
- 2027-12-11 11:20 PST — metrics show p95 returned to baseline (~240ms) and 5xx rate fell below 0.5% within 15 minutes

Customer impact: transient errors (~7% 5xx at peak) and degraded latency for ~35 minutes; higher-tier customers reported minor request failures during the window. Lumenity accepted mitigation and reported no data loss.

Action items and recommended next steps (owner in parens):
1) Postmortem within 3 business days including correlation of retry storm origin and mitigation (Redwood / Lumenity joint) (Rafael + Elena)
2) Provide a targeted KV prefix plan (requires request fingerprints from Lumenity) and implement persistent warming rules for frequent keys (Marissa)
3) Implement a safe default concurrency cap and kernel-fallback A/B experiment across private bundles to reduce single-shard amplification risk (Marissa / Markus)
4) Offer Lumenity an incident goodwill credit equivalent to one week of Dedicated smoothing for the impacted shard while we complete the postmortem (discuss with finance) (Laura)
5) Update onboarding docs to recommend client-side retry backoff and idempotency safeguards to prevent retry storms (Customer Success + Solutions)

Attachments included with this thread: lumenity-error-sample-logs.tar.gz, p95-cpu-traces.png, ma-tuning-proposal.docx

Thoughts on the credit offer: Laura, if you agree I can propose a one-week Dedicated smoothing credit and include it in the postmortem. Markus — we should prioritize the kernel-fallback experiment; this incident shows the cost of not having that widely enabled as a safe default.

Rafael Mendes
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0132
